gaps.why_now: The shared Phase 10 build step is the narrowest honest place to keep the virtio_mmio survey reviewable without claiming a transport implementation.

The existing virtio core lab slice already covers status negotiation, queue callback bookkeeping, bounded queue descriptor-shape metadata, and notification accounting, so the MMIO lane should build on that real foothold instead of inventing a second core starter.
The existing ring survey keeps the queue-wrapper roadmap gap explicit, which the MMIO lane depends on before transport-facing work can honestly begin.

The live repo now has a tiny in-memory virtqueue helper for queue shape, notification bookkeeping, used-buffer polling, callback re-enable state, and delayed-callback pacing, so the MMIO lane can survey the remaining transport gap against a real queue-facing foothold.
The ring slice note records the bounded queue-helper surface and its remaining non-goals, which keeps the MMIO lane from overstating transport readiness.
A dedicated MMIO survey gate makes the transport gap explicit and reviewable while `drivers/virtio/virtio_mmio.zig` is still intentionally absent.
The lane needs a Phase 10 note that records the current MMIO transport scope and the reasons the broader transport lifecycle work is still blocked behind a smaller register-window starter.
The live virtio_ring helper now covers queue shape, used-buffer polling, callback re-enable, and delayed-callback pacing, so the MMIO lane no longer needs to hold the ring-local follow-up open.

The roadmap requires virtqueue wrappers ahead of MMIO work, and that prerequisite is now satisfied by the landed virtio_ring delayed-callback pacing step, so the next honest bounded follow-up is one small register-window helper rather than more queue-local work.

Broader `virtio_mmio.c` parity still mixes interrupt acknowledgement, queue setup, reset, and probe or remove lifecycle paths, which remain too transport-facing to claim before a first register-window helper lands and gets reviewed.
